html:
SMTO-TSK-0043 — The new order didn't match the tasks that are waiting

GUID: 313325d8-6601-4628-b6a9-dd9ca373bcf8
Slug: task-queue-reorder-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The new order you asked for left out a waiting task or listed one twice, usually because a task was added or started meanwhile. Nothing was reordered.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page so the Queued list shows exactly the tasks waiting now. A task was probably added, started or removed after the list loaded.
  2. Move the task again with its ↑ (Move up) or ↓ (Move down) button. These buttons send the whole current list, so the new order will match.
  3. If a script reorders the list, have it send every waiting task exactly once, in the new order. SMTO only accepts an order that includes all waiting tasks with no repeats.

What success looks like

  • The Queued list shows the tasks in your new order.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete and re-add tasks just to change their order; they would lose their place and be created again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Reorder was rejected because the submitted task IDs repeat an ID or are not exactly the current set of future queued tasks.

What this means

  • A reorder list repeats task IDs or differs from the complete set of current future queued task IDs. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A reorder list repeats task IDs or differs from the complete set of current future queued task IDs.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare proposed IDs with the current future queue exactly, not with active or historical tasks.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the lane's queued_tasks and submit a reorder containing every current future task ID exactly once (excluding the active task and history), together with the current lane version.
  • Refresh the future queue and include every current future task exactly once in the desired order.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every current future task occurs exactly once in the submitted order.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
